request.question: Why did EBITDA per tonne change last quarter?

answer:
**EBITDA per tonne fell by 0.3 USD/t in Q1 FY2027 compared to Q4 FY2026, driven primarily by a 5.1 USD/t rise in FOB revenue that was largely offset by a 2.3 USD/t increase in royalties and a 0.2 USD/t increase in C1 cash cost.**

| Line Item | Q4 FY2026 (USD/t) | Q1 FY2027 (USD/t) | Change (USD/t) | Period | Source |
|-----------|-------------------|-------------------|----------------|--------|--------|
| FOB revenue | 104.71 | 109.82 | +5.11 | Per tonne shipped | SAP_STANDIN (BillingDocument) |
| Royalties (7.5% of FOB) | -7.85 | -8.24 | -0.38 | Per tonne shipped | SAP_STANDIN (BillingDocument) |
| C1 cash cost | -20.88 | -21.09 | -0.21 | Per tonne shipped | MIXED (SAP BDC + Operations) |
| Demurrage | -0.05 | -0.06 | -0.01 | Per tonne shipped | OPS (Port system) |
| **EBITDA** | **75.93** | **80.44** | **+4.51** | **Per tonne shipped** | **MIXED** |

*Correction: EBITDA per tonne actually increased by 4.5 USD/t, not decreased. The improvement was driven by the higher FOB revenue (+5.11 USD/t) exceeding the combined impact of increased royalties (-0.38 USD/t), C1 costs (-0.21 USD/t), and minimal demurrage increase (-0.01 USD/t).*

**Next step:** Investigate what drove the FOB revenue improvement—whether it reflects better market pricing or product mix—to sustain this margin gain.

---

**Sources:**  
*This data is simulated.*

**SAP_STANDIN:** BillingDocument (CFR revenue, ocean freight, FOB revenue, royalties)  
**MIXED:** Stand-in cost postings, SAP BDC, Operations (C1 cash cost, EBITDA)  
**OPS:** Port system (Demurrage)
